transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-22
Start: 16:00 PT
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Lena Patel (CTO, Sybaris Edge), Marcus Holt (Platform Eng), Priya Singh (Security), Devon (Product PM)

Summary: quick intro, TTFT priorities, security and deployment constraints, agree to pilot/benchmarks and SE deep dive.

--- OPTIONAL: Action items noted inline ---

00:00 Lena: Okay going to start, thanks everyone for joining. We are short on time so want to cover our key constraints which are privacy, and speed to first call, and then understand Redwood hosting options.
00:14 Ava: Thanks Lena. Hi all, I'm Ava, I'm the AE here. Marco is our solutions engineer. We'll walk through a quick overview and then dig into any security or infra questions. This is discovery so feel free to interrupt.
00:27 Marcus: Quick note, we already tried a few public APIs but the latency at scale is what killed us, so curious about TTFT and also whether we can do private deployment for PII workloads.
00:40 Marco: Totally. When you say TTFT are you asking about the time to get a token in dev env or production latency SLOs? sometimes folks mix those.
00:48 Lena: Both. The immediate need is for our dev teams to spin up the 1st call in an hour if possible from the SDK and then longer-term we need sub-200ms median token latency for the user-facing path.
01:02 Ava: Got it. Our PLG quickstart usually gets customers to first token in under 30 minutes — that's signup, API key, and a sample curl/SDK request using our hosted Redwood API. We also give 10k free credits for evaluation — that covers a few thousand requests depending on payload.
01:18 Priya: When you say hosted, what does data residency and logs look like? We need to ensure no raw customer data is persisted beyond X days and audit logs are available to us.
01:30 Marco: Good Q. Hosted does keep request traces for troubleshooting; retention and redaction are configurable per account. We provide audit logs exports and you can pull them into your SIEM. For stricter requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private where you control the VPC and KMS.
01:45 Priya: Does Redwood Hosted support customer-managed keys? We need keys that are not accessible to third parties.
01:51 Marco: Hosted by default uses Redwood-managed KMS, but we do have options for Bring Your Own Key when you move to Dedicated or Private; in Private you can fully integrate with your HSM.
02:05 Devon: What's the usual path people take — start hosted for speed then move to Dedicated?
02:10 Ava: Exactly — many teams onboard via hosted quickstart for developer velocity, then shift to Dedicated when they need dedicated capacity or customer-managed keys and stricter network controls.
02:22 Marcus: For Dedicated, are GPUs pinned or shared? Our concern is noisy neighbors and burst patterns from other tenants.
02:30 Marco: Dedicated reserves GPU pools for you; you get predictable throughput and isolation. You can configure autoscaling policies and burst capacity if you expect spikes.
02:41 Lena: Back to the TTFT: what's the actual sequence for a developer — sign up, get key, run sample, get to first token? How many steps?
02:52 Ava: Sign up, confirm email, create API key in console, copy curl/SDK snippet. We have SDKs in Node/Python and a one-file example that does a single request. Most devs see the first token within minutes; to fully instrument workloads and connect to internal CI it's usually a few hours.
03:08 Marcus: Is there a sandbox environment so we don't hit rate limits against prod?
03:12 Marco: The free credits are in a sandbox project by default; you get a quota. For larger pilots we can allocate dedicated pilot capacity.
03:19 Priya: On auditability — do you store full request payloads in logs? If so, can we request redaction?
03:26 Marco: By default we retain request metadata and truncated payloads for debugging. We support automatic redaction rules and field-level redaction for PII on Dedicated/Private deployments. For hosted we can set retention and redaction policies but if you need zero retention then Private is the path.
03:42 Lena: We have some air-gapped customers — would Redwood Private support an on-prem install?
03:48 Marco: Yes, Private can be deployed on-prem or in a customer-controlled VPC; it's our full control plane with optional air-gapped packaging. That comes with an enterprise license and on-site support.
03:59 Devon: Pricing — is the quickstart free forever? How do credits work?
04:06 Ava: The initial credits are promotional for evaluation. After credits expire we move to usage-based billing for hosted (per-token charges) or committed monthly for Dedicated. We'll send a pricing sheet with sample unit economics based on your expected qps and sequence lengths.
04:20 Marcus: Can you share an example of token cost and typical latency for a mid-sized model?
04:27 Marco: Sure — example: on our verified open model X with int8 quantization you'll see medians around 120–220ms for single-token response at low concurrency; cost per 1k tokens varies but we'll share a chart. For high throughput we recommend batching at the request layer and KV caching for prefixes.
04:47 Priya: You mentioned KV cache — is that something hosted supports? Where's the cache stored?
04:53 Marco: Yes hosted supports prefix and KV cache; data is stored in our managed cache for hosted, and in Dedicated/Private you can control cache eviction and storage. Cache helps reduce tokenization cost for repeated prefixes (like chat histories).
05:06 Lena: We're evaluating both speed and privacy; our immediate experiment is to replace a noisy vendor with something faster and cheaper. Who at Redwood would own a short benchmark?
05:15 Ava: Marco will run the bench plan with you — we'll need sample payloads, typical prompt lengths, concurrency targets, and your success metric.
05:22 Marcus: Ok we'll share a test corpus with a couple of traffic shapes: 1) chat-like 250 tokens, 2) summarization 1200 tokens, and 3) short rewrite 60 tokens. We want median p50/p95 and cost per 1M tokens.
05:39 Marco: Perfect. We'll backfill the plan and run host vs dedicated comparisons if you want. For hosted we can run baseline on our production fleet; for Dedicated we can provision pilot capacity.
05:50 Priya: What about SSO and RBAC? We need SAML SSO and granular roles.
05:55 Marco: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM provisioning; RBAC includes project-level roles, model-level permissions, and audit trails. Those are standard on Dedicated and Private; hosted supports SSO for enterprise tiers.
06:07 Lena: Any caveats around bringing our own models? We might bring a fine-tuned variant.
06:12 Marco: We support customer models on Dedicated/Private options — you can upload in the private registry and pin rollout policies. Hosted supports a curated catalog and limited BYO on request.
06:22 Devon: We have a compliance review next month. Can you provide SOC 2 and encryption docs?
06:28 Ava: Yes — we'll send SOC2, pen-test summary, architecture diagrams, and our KMS/audit docs.
06:34 Priya: Also need to know the logging schema so we can tell our auditors.
06:38 Marco: We'll include sample log schema and retention options in the package.
06:42 Lena: For the pilot timeline: we want to run a 3-week pilot, ideally starting in early August if we can get the quickstart and credits now. Is that realistic?
06:52 Ava: Yes that's realistic. We'll provision credits and a pilot account. After the pilot we can discuss Dedicated pilot capacity if needed.
07:00 Marcus: About network controls: can we set up VPC peering or private networking so traffic doesn't traverse public internet?
07:07 Marco: For Dedicated we offer VPC peering and private ingress. For hosted we have region-level isolation but not full VPC peering. Private gives full customer-controlled networking.
07:18 Priya: What does the rollout look like if we want canary/automatic fallback on model regressions?
07:24 Marco: We have rollout policies—canary deployments, percentage-based rollouts, and automatic fallback to a safe variant if metrics degrade. Those are part of the Redwood Console.
07:35 Devon: Can you show a very quick demo of the SDK flow? Even a 2-min snippet would help our devs understand the path.
07:41 Ava: We can, Marco do you want to show the snippet?
07:43 Marco: Sure. I'll paste the Node example in the chat: const client = new RedwoodClient({apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}); const res = await client.text.generate({model: 'open-compact-v1', input: 'Summarize...'}); console.log(res.output[0].content);

08:05 Marcus: That looks straightforward. When you say open-compact-v1 is that quantized?
08:09 Marco: It's a 16-bit optimized variant with quantization-friendly kernels; we list performance profiles on the catalog.

[transcription artifacts: small mis-hears and speaker label swaps near 09:00-14:00]

09:12 Priya: Quick question — how do you handle support for regulated industries, like healthcare?
09:18 Ava: We have compliance add-ons and can provide HIPAA support on Private deployments with BAAs — requires dedicated contract.
09:27 Marcus: For the benchmark, do you need us to run load from our lab or will Redwood run it?
09:33 Marco: We can do both. Usually we run a controlled benchmark from our infra to show baseline and then you run an in-situ test in your environment.
09:41 Lena: One more on costs — can you approximate monthly committed spend for Dedicated for 100 qps?
09:49 Ava: We have example pricing ranges; I'll send a sample estimate with variables: model family, sequence length, and desired latency SLO. Committed pricing often includes a discount vs hosted and predictable throughput guarantees.
09:59 Priya: Do you have any references of customers who moved from hosted to Dedicated for privacy reasons?
10:05 Ava: Yes, we can connect you with a couple of anonymized refs.
10:10 Devon: Any immediate blockers we should be aware of?
10:13 Priya: We'll need to confirm whether any of our data flows require on-prem processing. If so, Private is the likely path and needs procurement lead time.
10:22 Ava: Understood. We'll prepare options for both hosted quickstart and Dedicated pilot so you can choose based on the security review.

[rough sync — mid-call recaps and quick clarifications, some overlaps]

25:30 Marco: Quick recap of what's actionable: 1) We run a benchmark plan with your test corpus, 2) Redwood sends security + pricing docs, 3) Schedule SE deep-dive next week for Marcus, 4) Provide the 10k credits to the pilot project.
25:48 Lena: Sounds good. Who will own the benchmark updates?
25:52 Marco: I'll own it — Marco Ruiz. I'll include p50/p95, cost per 1M tokens, and memory/kv-cache settings.
26:02 Priya: Please include the log schema and sample retention settings in the security packet.
26:07 Ava: Will do.

36:10 Marcus: One last engineering question — are there rate-limit headers and cost-estimation hooks so we can instrument our client?
36:16 Marco: Yes we return usage headers per request and you can also query usage endpoints for aggregated cost. We also support token-level breakdown for debugging.
36:26 Devon: Great. For the pilot, is there a minimum contract?
36:31 Ava: For hosted pilot with credits no minimum. For Dedicated pilot we typically ask for a short-term reserved pilot agreement but we can be flexible.
36:40 Lena: Okay that's helpful. We're aiming to start the pilot the week of Aug 3. We'll circulate internal stakeholders.
36:47 Ava: Perfect — we'll get the docs out today and set up the SE deep dive.

46:00 Ava: Recap — I'll send quickstart and pricing, Marco will draft the benchmark plan and security packet, Priya will send compliance constraints, Lena will confirm pilot stakeholders and timeline. Any final Qs?
46:15 Priya: No, that's all from security for now.
46:20 Marcus: No from infra.
46:23 Lena: Thank you, this was useful.
46:28 Ava: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD with the docs and the credits.
46:33 Meeting end.
